title: 1-minute prep
intro: Three questions to ask, one thing to avoid, one thing to remember. Read it on your way in.

cards.title: Regular 1:1
ask: How are you doing, really?
What's going well, and what's getting in the way?
What do you need from me before we next meet?
cards.avoid: Don't let it turn into a status update. Their agenda comes first.
cards.remember: Check the actions you agreed last time.

cards.title: Return to work
ask: How are you feeling now?
Is there anything we should do to help you settle back in?
Did anything at work contribute to the absence?
cards.avoid: Don't ask for more medical detail than you need.
cards.remember: Hold it on their first day back if you can.

cards.title: Probation review
ask: How do you feel the role is going so far?
What's been hardest to get to grips with?
What support would help you meet the standard?
cards.avoid: Don't let a concern come up for the first time at the final review.
cards.remember: Know the possible outcomes before you go in.

cards.title: Performance review
ask: What are you most proud of this period?
Where do you think things fell short, and why?
What do you want to develop next?
cards.avoid: Don't bring up criticism that hasn't been raised during the year.
cards.remember: Bring their objectives and a few specific examples.

cards.title: Stay interview
ask: What do you look forward to at work?
What might tempt you to leave?
What's one thing I could change to make your job better?
cards.avoid: Don't get defensive, or promise what you can't deliver.
cards.remember: Follow through on what you say you'll do.

cards.title: New starter check-in
ask: How are you settling in?
Is there anything you still need that you don't have?
Is anything different from what you expected?
cards.avoid: Don't assume that no questions means no problems.
cards.remember: Check in at week 1, month 1 and month 3.

cards.title: Underperformance
ask: How do you think things have been going?
Is anything getting in the way: workload, training, tools, or anything outside work?
What would help you improve here?
cards.avoid: Don't generalise with "always" or "never". Use specific examples.
cards.remember: Have 2 or 3 dated examples ready.

cards.title: Lateness and timekeeping
ask: Is there anything behind this that I should know about?
Is anything making the start time difficult?
What can we agree from here?
cards.avoid: Don't raise it in front of colleagues.
cards.remember: Bring the dates and their contracted hours.

cards.title: Behaviour and conduct
ask: Can you talk me through what happened from your point of view?
How do you think it came across to others?
What will you do differently from now on?
cards.avoid: Don't reach a conclusion before you've heard their account.
cards.remember: If it's serious, talk to HR before you do anything else.

cards.title: Conflict between team members
ask: How do things look from your side?
What do you need from [colleague] to work well together?
Would you be willing to meet together?
cards.avoid: Don't take sides.
cards.remember: Speak to each person on their own first.

cards.title: Frequent short-term absence
ask: Is there an underlying reason, or anything that connects these absences?
Is anything at work contributing?
What support would help?
cards.avoid: Don't suggest they're not genuinely ill.
cards.remember: Have the absence record to hand, and check your policy.

cards.title: Mental health
ask: How are you doing?
How is it affecting you at work?
What would help right now?
cards.avoid: Don't diagnose or give opinions about conditions.
cards.remember: Know where to point them: your Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), their GP or Occupational Health (OH). If there's a risk to life, call 999.

cards.title: Bereavement
ask: How are you doing?
How much time do you think you need?
How would you like us to keep in touch?
cards.avoid: Don't push for a return date.
cards.remember: Keep the first conversation short and kind.

cards.title: Menopause
ask: How is it affecting you at work?
What adjustments would help?
When shall we review how it's going?
cards.avoid: Don't make jokes, assumptions or comments about age.
cards.remember: They only need to share what they're comfortable with.

cards.title: Pregnancy announcement
ask: How are you feeling?
Who knows, and when would you like the team told?
Is there anything you need right now?
cards.avoid: Don't ask whether they plan to come back.
cards.remember: A risk assessment is needed, and HR will cover leave and pay.

cards.title: Personal hygiene
ask: Is there anything that might be contributing to this?
Is there anything I can do to help?
Is there anything you'd like to ask me?
cards.avoid: Don't drop hints or drag it out. Be direct, brief and kind.
cards.remember: Find a private place and a quiet moment.

cards.title: Giving feedback
ask: How did you see it?
What would you do differently next time?
What support would help?
cards.avoid: Don't sandwich the message between compliments.
cards.remember: Situation, Behaviour, Impact.

cards.title: Saying no to a request
ask: What matters most to you about this request?
Would any of these alternatives work for you?
What would you like to happen next?
cards.avoid: Don't blame others if it's your decision.
cards.remember: Give the honest reason, and what would need to change for a yes.

cards.title: Flexible working request
ask: What exactly are you looking for?
How do you see it working day to day?
Would a trial period work for you?
cards.avoid: Don't refuse in the meeting before you've considered it properly.
cards.remember: They don't have to give a reason. Know when the written decision is due.

cards.title: Pay rise request
ask: What do you think justifies the increase?
What are you hoping for?
If it's not possible now, what would you like to work towards?
cards.avoid: Don't promise an increase you can't approve.
cards.remember: Know how and when pay decisions are made.

cards.title: Announcing change
ask: What questions do you have?
How do you feel about it?
What would help you through the change?
cards.avoid: Don't speculate or share rumours.
cards.remember: Be clear on what's changing, why, when, and how it affects them.

cards.title: Grievance raised
ask: What happened, in your own words?
What would you like to happen next?
Would you like this to be dealt with formally?
cards.avoid: Don't investigate or reach a view yourself.
cards.remember: Pass it to HR the same day if you can.

cards.title: Harassment or bullying complaint
ask: Can you tell me what happened?
Do you feel safe at work right now?
Is there anything you need straight away?
cards.avoid: Don't confront the person accused or promise confidentiality.
cards.remember: Contact HR straight away. If anyone is in immediate danger, call 999.

cards.title: Suspected impairment at work
ask: Are you OK?
Have you taken any medication today?
Who can help you get home safely?
cards.avoid: Don't let them drive or carry on with safety-critical work.
cards.remember: Safety first, then HR.

cards.title: Redundancy or restructure
ask: What questions do you have?
How are you feeling about it?
What support would help?
cards.avoid: Don't speculate or promise who will be affected.
cards.remember: Only share what HR has approved, when they agree.

cards.title: Poor team morale
ask: What's going well at the moment?
What's making things hard?
What one thing would make the biggest difference?
cards.avoid: Don't get defensive.
cards.remember: Agree a small change, then report back on it.

cards.title: Managing a former peer
ask: How are you feeling about the change?
What would help you most from me?
What are your goals for the next year?
cards.avoid: Don't share confidential information with former close colleagues.
cards.remember: Be fair and consistent with everyone.
